newsitem.title: IRAN: Tajik government, opposition sign accord in Iran.
newsitem.headline: Tajik government, opposition sign accord in Iran.

text.p: Tajikistan's government and opposition signed an accord in Iran on Wednesday which opens the way for a peace agreement next month to end the former Soviet republic's civil war, Iranian media and the United Nations said.

Tajik Foreign Minister Talbak Nazarov and deputy opposition leader Akbar Turojonzada signed the document which guarantees the implementation of earlier agreements between the two sides, the United Nations Information Centre in Tehran said.

The accord, also signed by U.N. special envoy Gerd Merrem, completed inter-Tajik talks and opened the way for the signing of the final deal by Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov and opposition leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri in Moscow, the U.N office said in a statement.
Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati, who attended the talks, told Tehran radio the Moscow signing would take place "in the next two or three weeks".
Rakhmonov and Nuri earlier this month took a big step towards ending the four-year civil war by signing an accord legalising major Islamist opposition parties and media.
After talks in Kyrgyzstan, they also agreed on an amnesty and exchange of prisoners.
Last December, Rakhmonov's secular government and the Islamists agreed a ceasefire in a war which killed tens of thousands of people in the Central Asian state and drove many more from their homes.
Military terms for the peace deal and a power-sharing agreement have also been agreed.
